text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: P1 — Multi-region failover trouble detected. Automated traffic shift started us-east-1 -> us-west-1 at 2026-03-15T03:00Z. ~40% of requests returning 502/timeout. Route53 health checks showing inconsistent propagation. Pager triggered. https://internal.incidents/1762510001
elena: I'm on call and will lead. Quick check: control plane healthy in us-west, instances are registered but ELB reports many targets Unhealthy. Possible healthcheck mismatch or network filter.
andre: ack, pulling ELB logs and node health.
marcos: seen traceroutes from monitoring -> us-west1 with packet loss at provider edge, AS path jumps between peering POPs. Might be routing flap but let's confirm local config first.
infra-bot: Auto-rollout paused: canary halted for deployment web-proxy in us-east-1.
hana: customer-impact: 37 customers reporting timeouts via our support dashboard; high severity for a subset (fintech-prod, search-api). Flagging SLO risk.
elena: running quick probes and commands now:
```
kubectl get pods -n web -o wide --selector=app=web-proxy
curl -sS -D- http://10.12.45.67/health | head -n 50
dig +short prod.redwoodapi.com @8.8.8.8
```
andre: curl directly to node IP returns 200 OK. LB healthcheck endpoint returns 503 from the LB perspective. nginx access logs show healthcheck user-agent "ELB-HealthChecker" receiving 504s.
marcos: tcpdump on LB subnet shows SYNs from healthcheck IPs but intermittent no SYN-ACK — looks like a RST or DROP in path.
elena: hypothesis: nodes are healthy when probed locally, but health checks from other AZs/ELB IP ranges are being dropped by a host firewall or NACL (asymmetric routing). Checking iptables and recent hardening changes.
andre: searching config change history... found a host-level iptables rule added ~02:10Z by hardening job that drops 54.243.0.0/16 (AWS ELB addr space) on several web-proxy nodes in us-west1. That matches timeline.
hana: if healthchecks come from 54.x ranges, that would explain only failing during failover when LB probes from different AZ IPs.
elena: removing rule and restarting services now. Commands:
```
ssh node-55
sudo iptables -D INPUT -s 54.243.0.0/16 -j DROP || true
sudo systemctl restart nginx
```
infra-bot: firewall rule removal action recorded for node-55 by elena.
andre: ELB healthchecks are flipping back to healthy on 3/5 nodes; traffic shift resumed. Observability: 95% of traffic successfully failing over now. :white_check_mark:
hana: customer-impact update: affected customers down to 6, support volume returned to normal. We estimate ~12 minutes of degraded for major accounts. Logging for billing/credits.
elena: root cause summary: hardening script introduced iptables DROP for ELB IP range on web-proxy nodes in us-west1. During automated multi-region failover, LB healthchecks originated from those IPs, caused targets to be marked unhealthy and traffic stayed in source region, leading to partial failures. Mitigation: removed iptables rule, restarted nginx, validated healthchecks and resumed traffic shift.
elena: handoff to oncall-next for follow-up, RCA and postmortem. Immediate action items: revert hardening release for web-proxy, add CI integration test that simulates cross-AZ healthchecks, add explicit allow rules for ELB/healthcheck IP ranges in the hardened baseline, update region-drain runbook to include healthcheck verification step.
oncall-next: ack taking over. I'll own RCA and coordinate with security + infra to patch the hardening script and add CI tests. ETA 24h for RCA draft.
customer-success: prepping outbound for impacted enterprise customers and posting interim update. Suggested language: apology, summary of cause and mitigation, credits offer. Posting to #customer-comm now.
marcos: I'll own postmortem doc and link tests/commands we ran. Also will propose a canary validator job that simulates failovers pre-merge.
elena: tagging follow-ups: @security for hardening script, @devex for CI test, @sre for runbook update. Closing incident channel once RCA linked. :thumbsup:
